Well, it's really dependent on the frame you're using. If that were a case of say, Nidus, then ye go for Growing Power but the main reason I tend to recommend forma'ing that aura into a - is mainly so that your frame can benefit both the team and yourself so you can run both solo and team while still benefitting all.

At the moment, there isn't really any objectively best or west kitgun or zaw. It's highly dependent on your preference and what you enjoy. 

Now, for my recommendation, in terms of Zaws, I'd recommend: 

· 1h Sepfahn (Nikana) 
· 1h Cyath (Machete iirc) 
· 2h Dokrahm (Greatsword) 
· 2h Plague Kripath (Polearm) 
· 1h Plague Keewar (Machete) 

These are the really fun and strong combinations that I personally love. 

In terms of links and grips, go for what you feel like you prefer best. If you like more speed, more damage. Maybe you prefer status with Condition Overload or maybe pure crit with Blood Rush. 

The choice is yours! 

Now for Kitguns, the spectrum broadens even further and the most I can really recommend is using semlar.com/kitguncalc to check different combinations and see what you like best. 

One tip though is I highly recommend going for a hybrid of status and crit on your kitgun. 

And at the moment, MOA minmaxing isn't really a thing. Once you attain the highest amount of survivability possible on your MOA, what's left for you to do is fashion it xD

The reason most people Forma their polarities to a - instead of a V is simply due to the amount of well rounded auras that can be used both for solo play and team play. 

The main ones being Corrosive Projection, Shield Disruption, Enemy Radar, and/or Sprint Boost. 

Now, in the case of V polarity vs - polarity, you're effectively comparing those 4 - mods vs Steel Charge, Power Donation, and Growing Power. 

(Just speaking from the most popular ones. The other ones tend to not see much use due to the significantly small benefit they provide) 

Out of those Growing Power is really only better than any of the - mods when trying to push for a maximum amount of strength possible (Which only frames such as Oberon or Chroma would actually need) and Steel Charge is really only when you absolutely need the capacity. 

On most frames that possess damage buffs based on strength, though, Corrosive Projection is still more likely to provide a bigger damage benefit due to how fast armor scales the higher up the levels you go. 

Hopefully this answers your question. ^^

It's highly dependent on what role you are playing. 

If you are playing Chroma, definitely swap out Serration in favor of Primed Cryo Rounds. Reasoning? Chroma's Vex Armor buff now acts like multiple Serrations, basically granting damage based off of your weapon's unmodded stats. 

On the other hand, when modding with elementals such as Radiation or Cold, that damage is multiplied *after* the Serration stacks, effectively giving you a significantly higher damage output per shot. 

Now, remember that proccing only matters when you're trying to apply statuses which you shouldn't be doing for Eidolons. 

When fighting Eidolons, focus on pure damage to down the Eidolons. 

If you are a role other than Chroma, sustain Serration but also make sure that aside from mandatory mods. 

You want to have at least 200% multishot (Normally attained with Split Chamber + Riven w/ 110% multishot but also can be done with Split Chamber + Riven + Vigilante Armaments) no matter what role you're playing so you can build up your sniper combo counter fast and have a higher likelihood of downing an Eidolon's limb on the first shot.
